        Hurricanes Isaias has affected travel plans around the country, and that includes President Donald Trump. Originally, Trump planned to be in attendance when No. 2 Georgia faced No. 6 Alabama in Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, but the Tuscaloosa Police Department told AL.com that he scrapped the trip due to the impending storm.Trump has attended several Alabama football games throughout his tenure, and he's friendly with legendary coach Nick Saban, who has expressed support for Trump as it pertains to the Protect College Sports Act.In 2018, Trump made the trip down to Atlanta for the College Playoff National Championship, which the Crimson Tide won due to overtime heroics from Tua Tagovailoa. The next year, in 2019, Trump was at Bryant-Denny Stadium for the shootout that was LSU vs. Alabama.While weather may have nixed this trip, Trump has gotten to watch a little college football in person this season. He was in Knoxville just two weeks ago when Texas triumphed over Tennessee, 20-17.
For the moment, Hurricanes Isaias isn't expected to change much about the game itself. Both teams are planning to play on Saturday night in Tuscaloosa as scheduled, but the SEC is monitoring the storm and the kickoff time could be altered slightly.The storm is expected to bring locally heavy rain, potential flooding, high winds and isolated tornadoes throughout the Southeast this weekend, although the exact path is still unknown.According to both coaches, the teams are preparing as normal for the game, since the weather is well outside of their control. Wet-ball drills and mental preparation are all that can be done for now.
"Depends on the level of weather you get, it would affect what happens," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said, according to 247Sports. "It's just -- that's not my area of expertise. I'm just getting our football team ready. It hasn't affected us much, other than we're doing wet ball drills and get wet ball involved in some of our team reps, just like we did last week at times, preparing for the rain a week ago. I'm not really involved in too much."

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a number of different wagering options available on each race, and here we will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that define bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.           Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will even allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           These are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        It's a must-have for both teams, as No. 19 USC hits the road to take on Penn State Saturday night in Happy Valley.Penn State enters the game with its season seemingly spiraling out of control. After a 3-0 start in nonconference play under new coach Matt Campbell, the Nittany Lions have dropped their first two Big Ten games, and didn't look particularly inspiring in either. The offense struggled mightily in losses to Wisconsin and Northwestern, and last week, the defense was gashed by Northwestern's rushing attack.Suddenly, a schedule that was considered one of the easiest in the Big Ten before the season began looks far more difficult for the Nittany Lions.Not that things have been much easier for their opponents. The Trojans are 5-1 on the season and are coming off a win, but have looked shaky for three straight games. They found themselves in a shootout with Rutgers three weeks ago, followed that up with a 14-point home loss to Oregon, and last week flirted with disaster against a Washington team that hadn't looked impressive to start the season.
Now they're on the road against a team with its back against the wall, and a second loss (with Ohio State and Indiana still to come) could crush USC's playoff chances.USC vs. Penn State: Need to know  It's the White-Out game: Penn State's White-Out game is a newer tradition in college football, having begun in 2007, but it's quickly become one of the games Penn State fans look forward to most. Everybody in Beaver Stadium is dressed in white and screaming at their absolute loudest. Unfortunately, the results haven't always matched the intensity. Penn State is only 11-7 in White-Out games, but that's partly because the Nittany Lions reserve the tradition for their toughest games.  It's a battle of the two winningest QBs in college football: That fact probably caught you by surprise, didn't it? Well, it's true. Penn State's Rocco Becht comes into this game with 29 wins as a starting QB in his college career. That's more than any other QB in the country. USC's Jayden Maiava is tied for second with 24. So Becht will either widen the gap this week, or Maiava will narrow it.  
Penn State hoping to avoid a 0-3 start in Big Ten again: Last season, the Nittany Lions started 0-6 in Big Ten play. It was an unexpected slide that led to James Franklin's mid-season firing. If they lose here, they'll be 0-3 in the Big Ten for the second straight season. The last time that happened was the 2003 and 2004 seasons. Of course, Matt Campbell could take some solace if his team loses. He'd be the first Penn State full-time head coach to start his tenure with a 3-3 mark since Joe Paterno in 1966.Where to watch USC vs. Penn State live  Date: Saturday, October 10 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET  Location: Beaver Stadium -- University Park, Pennsylvania  TV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)USC vs. Penn State prediction, picks  I find myself in a rather precarious position here. I don't like either side of the total, so I'm being asked to back a Penn State team that's looked terrible lately as a favorite, or take a USC team that's really struggled on the road under Lincoln Riley as a small dog. Frankly, there's no right option here, and I don't recommend taking any side. But, unlike you, I don't have a choice, so I guess I'm less terrified of USC +1.5 than anything else. Pick: USC +1.5

        Two top-six teams will play Saturday night in Tuscaloosa and yet the potential impact of Hurricane Isaiah has overshadowed No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 Alabama. The hurricane, expected to make landfall on Friday, could bring significant bad weather to the state of Alabama on Saturday. It could even be as strong as a Category 2 hurricane – sustained wind speeds between 96 to 110 miles per hour – when it makes landfall on the Gulf Coast. Both schools and the SEC have been monitoring the situation but the game is still scheduled to kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night. Assuming it goes off as planned, it pits two of the SEC's premier teams against each other. There is plenty of history between the two schools as Alabama won a regular season game at Athens last season while Georgia avenged the loss with a win over the Crimson Tide in the SEC Championship.  Alabama is coming off a convincing 56-23 win on the road over then-No. 16 Mississippi State. Quarterback Keelon Russell, who has emerged as a Heisman Trophy favorite, was fantastic against the Bulldogs, throwing for 285 yards and three touchdowns on just 22 pass attempts.  
Georgia has crushed all its competition this season. The Bulldogs' lowest scoring output of the season came last week over Vanderbilt in what was still a 38-14 win. Georgia has the best scoring margin in the country with an average victory of 32.5 points. How much could Hurricane Isaias impact the game? It's one of the biggest looming questions of the weekend. Alabama has the nation's third-best scoring offense while Georgia ranks third in rushing defense, seventh in total defense and 12th in scoring defense. Alabama's run game is improved this season but still ranks only 44th nationally which could be a significant factor if the pass game is ineffective in poor weather conditions.   Alabama vs. Georgia: Need to know Leading TD rusher out: Georgia will be without running back Chauncey Bowens who leads the Bulldogs with six rushing touchdowns. Bowens has been especially valuable as a short-yardage back which could have come in handy in what might be rainy and messy conditions Saturday night. While his loss is significant, the good news is Georgia will likely have running back Nate Frazier back. Frazier missed the Oklahoma game and played sparingly in the Bulldogs' win over Vanderbilt last weekend. Frazier has been dealing with bruised ribs and should be in for a larger workload with Bowens out.  
He's trying to do what?!: Alabama starting tight end Josh Ford broke his arm against Mississippi State, an unfortunate development for the 6-foot-6 junior from Oklahoma. The crazy thing? He's still trying to play this weekend against Georgia. Ford was listed as questionable on Alabama's availability report, a wild development given he broke his arm less than a week ago. Ford isn't a huge part of the passing game -- he has one catch for one touchdown -- but plays a key role as a run-blocking tight end. That he even has a shot to play the game speaks to how tough a player the Oklahoma State transfer is.  CFP implications: Both teams are currently well-positioned to make the College Football Playoff. Georgia (93.1 percent) and Alabama (81.8 percent) have two of the five highest playoff odds, according to CBS Sports forecasting and projections. Even with a loss each team will still be in a good position to make a field. But with a win? It'd almost guarantee a spot. Georgia's odds would improve to 97.7 percent while Alabama's would jump to 93.5 percent.   Where to watch Alabama vs. Georgia live Date: Saturday, October 10 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET Location: Bryant-Denny Stadium -- Tuscaloosa, Alabama 
TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Alabama vs. Georgia prediction, picks Can Alabama really beat Georgia in three consecutive regular season games? Kalen DeBoer has had the edge over Kirby Smart in the regular season -- Georgia did, however, beat Alabama in last year's SEC Championship -- including in memorable fashion the last time the two teams played each other in Tuscaloosa. The weather conditions create the ultimate unknown but I think they tend to favor Georgia which isn't as reliant on its aerial passing attack. This one will be close as they always seem to be in the regular season, but the Bulldogs eke it out late.  Pick: Georgia +1.5

title: Knicks pause contract extension talks: Is Josh Hart's time in New York running out? - CBS Sports
description: Coming off a title, four Knicks players are eligible for contract extensions, including starters Karl-Anthony Tow
body:
Coming off a title, four Knicks players are eligible for contract extensions, including starters Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Only the New York Knicks could crush the vibes of a championship run before even beginning their title defense season. Four notable members of the team, Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek, are eligible for contract extensions. While keeping the whole team together was always going to be a long shot, the Knicks announced on Friday that they would be tabling all talks until later in the season, forcing all four players to open the season with uncertain financial futures.But what does this actually mean for the Knicks? Here are three quick takeaways on New York's sudden financial predicament.1. Knicks lose critical option on new Towns dealFor now, the question with Towns remains less about whether he'll get a new deal from the Knicks and more about what that new deal will mean for everyone else. Towns is irreplaceable. There is no other offensive center like him in basketball that has not already won an MVP or will inevitably win one in the near future. New York let its only other viable starting center option, Mitchell Robinson, leave in free agency, and as we've learned from deals involving players like Ivica Zubac and Walker Kessler, getting a high-end starter at center, even below the superstar level, costs draft capital the Knicks frankly do not have. They'll figure something out with Towns. It's just a matter of when and what.

        
            
                Knicks pause contract negotiations with Karl-Athony Towns, Josh Hart, others until 'later in the season'
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Knicks have hoped to get Towns to take a substantial discount, as Jalen Brunson has. While he seems receptive to taking a deal below his $276 million max, the Knicks have seemingly not come close to an actual deal for him. While Friday's news doesn't necessarily preclude a below-market agreement down the line, it does deprive the Knicks of a critical bit of flexibility in how that deal is structured.Players with multiple years left on their contracts cannot extend during the season. Before the season, however, extensions are fair game. This matters for Towns because he has a $61.6 million player option for the 2027-28 season. If Towns and the Knicks had gotten a deal done before the season, they could have essentially used that option to front-load Towns' new contract and have his salary decline meaningfully from there. However, should he sign an extension during the season, he would have to decline that option, and his new contract would have to be more balanced. A player's salary cannot increase or decrease by more than 8% annually within a single contract. Major raises and dips must be part of a new contract or extension.
Why is this a potentially preferred contract structure? Because New York's financial cliff isn't coming in the 2027-28 season. It comes a year later in the 2028-29 campaign. That's when Brunson and OG Anunoby will start new deals thanks to their player options. Brunson has already taken a substantial discount once. Don't expect him to do it again. Anunoby is about as irreplaceable as non-All-Stars get. Using that option, the Knicks could have gotten the most expensive year of a new Towns deal out of the way and saved as much flexibility for what comes after as possible.This format isn't necessarily off the table. Towns could simply pick up his player option in the offseason and try extension talks again at that point. His value could also dip during the season, allowing the Knicks to re-sign him on more favorable terms. But it's always easier to get an extension done early when possible. The last thing the Knicks should want is their back-to-back title bid ruined by contractual sour grapes. In a perfect world, the Knicks would have preferred to have something done by now. This might not be their preferred structure, as a lower 2027-28 salary would make it easier to duck next year's second apron. But taking the option off the table, if only temporarily, costs the Knicks the flexibility they would probably have preferred.
2. It's time to start questioning Hart's future in New YorkWe should assume that Brunson's next deal will approach 35% of the cap. His discount won the Knicks a championship. Towns won't be quite that high, but it won't be far off either. Anunoby's player option for the 2028-29 season will pay him an estimated 26.2% of the cap, so a new deal probably starts in that range. Mikal Bridges is locked up at around 21% of the estimated cap at that point. Start doing the math. You're looking at around 110 to 115% of the cap for your top four players once everyone's deals are finalized. You should also assume that those deals are paying for fewer valuable years than their existing contracts do. Anunoby is going into his age-29 season. Brunson and Anunoby will play their age-30 seasons this year, and Towns his age-31 season. At best, you're paying for the back half of their prime. At worst, there will be real age- and injury-related decline. If the Knicks are going to continue competing for championships, they need to acknowledge that they probably need more than they currently have to do it (especially with Robinson already gone) and that they have less financial wiggle room to pursue possible upgrades.So where does that leave Hart, the fifth starter and the heartbeat of the team? A lot depends on what sort of extension he's willing to take. The Knicks have a bit more flexibility on this front than with Towns because he has a team option rather than a player option. The Knicks could use that option to leverage their way into more favorable terms.
Still, Hart is the oldest of the five Knicks starters. He'll turn 32 during the season. His game is probably the least likely to age well, given his inconsistent shooting and borderline reckless physicality he plays with. The old axiom is that it's better to move on from a player a year too early than a year too late. It's hard to imagine the Knicks moving Hart this season as they pursue back-to-back titles, but hesitance on a long-term extension afterward would be understandable.There isn't an in-house replacement ready. The Knicks under two different head coaches have resisted playing McBride with the starters because of how small his backcourt pairing with Brunson would be. Landry Shamet's shooting is nice in small doses and he's improved significantly as a defender, but similar problems exist there, and durability has been a concern for him. Perhaps the best possible developmental curve for promising second-round pick Mohamed Diawara could see him turn into a starter, and he's locked into a cheap, long-term deal, but he's a long way from adequately replacing Hart.Realistically, the Knicks would either have to stumble into a player we don't see coming or make a trade involving their precious remaining draft capital (at this point, their only tradable first-rounder is in 2033), ideally for someone on a rookie deal now. This front office has surprised plenty of times, but at this moment, Hart is still essential to New York's championship upside. The more costly Towns becomes, though, the more realistic breaking up this starting lineup becomes. You can't keep everyone in the apron era, especially if you want to maintain any level of depth.
3. Deuce McBride is the likeliest trade candidateMcBride will almost certainly be the cheapest of the three Knicks we've covered thus far on his next deal. He certainly is on his existing contract. The Knicks wisely extended McBride on very team-friendly terms right after trading Immanuel Quickley, knowing that he had a bigger role upcoming. If they extend McBride before Hart, that might be a tell that they're considering repeating that process with him stepping into a starting role afterward.
In reality, though, we have to assume that Hart will be a higher priority than McBride. In that case, McBride represents an expiring contract at New York's deepest position. Not only do the Knicks have Shamet, Jose Alvarado and Kolek as viable backcourt reserves, but they have several veterans on camp deals (like Bruce Brown) fighting for a roster spot at that position as well. Meanwhile, the Knicks have very little center depth behind Towns, making McBride an obvious trade candidate to potentially fill that hole.The tell here will be who winds up getting the final roster spot for the Knicks and how the early season goes thereafter. Say the Knicks keep a big man like James Wiseman and he proves to be playable early in the year. At that point, trading for another big becomes less of a priority. If Brown or Ochai Agbaji make the team, however, the Knicks would be left with just Towns and Andre Drummond at center unless they make a move to clear another roster spot. In that world, a McBride trade seems more likely.

title: Dez Bryant calls out Cowboys for controversial two-point decision in fourth quarter: "Wasn't smart' - CBS Sports
description: Dez Bryant didn't like Dallas' call to go for two, and he may have been right
body:
Dez Bryant didn't like Dallas' call to go for two, and he may have been right
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Former Cowboys star Dez Bryant isn't a fan of analytics, at least not when it pertains to one specific scenario, and that exact situation came up during Dallas' stunning 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. With the Cowboys trailing 24-10 in the fourth quarter, Dak Prescott engineered a 99-yard drive that culminated with an 18-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens. After the score, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer decided to go for two, but the Cowboys came up short.  
Bryant shared his thoughts about the decision on social media, and he definitely didn't agree with Schottenheimer's choice to bypass an easy extra point. 
Dez better get used to the idea of the Cowboys doing this, because if this same situation comes up in the future, Dallas will definitely be going for two, and Schottenheimer made that clear after the game. 
"That's our philosophy," Schottenheimer said via Patrik Walker of the team's official website. "When you're down 14, especially with our offense, because when you get it, you have a chance to go and win the game, and you make it a six-point game."Bryant was clearly frustrated with the call, but Schottenheimer's decision came down to numbers, so let's break down both sides of the coin. Why the Cowboys went for twoThis all comes down to analytics. The math says it makes more sense to go for two when you score a touchdown while trailing by 14. The main reason teams do this is so they know what they need to get sooner rather than later. 
A two-point conversion has about a 50% chance of success if you look at the historical rate, while an extra point has about a 97% success rate. Since the Cowboys needed two scores to tie or take the lead, Schottenheimer had to plan ahead and decide what the team would do after each touchdown. With that in mind, he essentially had two options (this all assumes the game played out similarly to Thursday, with the Cowboys defense not giving up any more points): 1. Kick the extra point after each touchdown 2. Go for two after the first touchdown, and the result of that attempt would determine what the team would do on the second touchdown. If you convert the two-pointer, you kick the extra point on the second attempt. If you fail on the two-pointer, then you have to attempt a two-point conversion on your second attempt. 
If you go with option 1, that guarantees overtime. If you go with option 2, you have a chance to win in regulation. For the Cowboys specifically, option 2 likely had some appeal because the Bucs had been steamrolling their defense all night. If the Cowboys had converted the two-pointer, then Dallas' defense would have only had to make one more stop to give the Cowboys a chance to win the game. Now, let's run through all the numbers on the two-point decision: Two-pointer is successful on first TD plus a kicked extra point on second TD = 48.5% (In this scenario, you win in regulation)Two-pointer fails on first TD, second two-pointer is successful = 25% (In this scenario, the game goes to overtime)Two-pointer fails on first TD AND second TD = 25% (In this scenario, you lose)Successful extra point on both touchdowns = 94.1% (In this scenario, the game goes to overtime)If you kick two extra points, there's no scenario where you win in regulation, and that's part of the allure of the two-pointer. If you make the first one, you put your team in an advantageous situation, and that's what Schottenheimer was trying to do. Why Dez didn't like the decision, and why he might be rightAfter the game was over, Bryant offered a longer explanation for why he didn't like the two-point decision, and considering this take is coming from a former player, it's certainly worth listening to. 
"I don't care if we got the 2, I still think that wasn't a smart decision," Bryant wrote. "Knowing you're down 7 vs. down 8 makes a difference."Basically, there's a psychological aspect of the decision that the math doesn't account for. A player's mentality changes based on the score, especially late in the game. If you watch a highlight of the Cowboys' two-point attempt, Dak Prescott and several other players walked off the field with a dejected look after the conversion failed. This team just drove 99 yards for a huge touchdown, but it felt like they lost momentum after the failed two-point conversion. Not only is there a psychological aspect to consider, but there's also the overtime aspect. In general, teams want to win in regulation because, in the past, overtime would essentially come down to a coin flip. If you won the coin toss, you got the ball, and you could go down and win the game with a touchdown. However, with the new overtime rules, both teams are guaranteed a possession, so if you force overtime, you know your best unit — in Dallas' case, that would be the offense — will get to see the field at least once. 
The time left in the game should also play into a coach's consideration. If the Cowboys had scored with 2:30 left, it probably wouldn't make sense to go for two, because if you fail, you're now in a situation where you might need TWO more possessions to win, which is what would happen if you also failed on the second two-pointer. In that situation, your opponent would get two possessions, and they would be able to burn off a minimum of two minutes without getting a single first down. Also, if you miss the first two-point conversion, you're down eight, which means you have to score quickly, because you have to leave yourself some time in case you miss the second two-point conversion. And if you do miss, then your defense has to make ANOTHER stop. I get the math of going for two in the Cowboys' situation, but this shouldn't be an automatic play. As Bryant pointed out, there are other factors at play besides the raw numbers, so teams should probably make case-by-case decisions rather than make it their "philosophy."

        The Baltimore Ravens will be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson when the team travels to Atlanta to take on the red-hot Falcons, as he has been ruled out with an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will start under center as Baltimore looks to improve on its 3-1 record.Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters they knew Jackson being ruled out for Week 5 was always a possibility, but that the quarterback worked "his tail off" in recovery, and is "doing everything in his power to get back." He did not practice at all this week. The two-time NFL MVP injured his ankle at the end of the second quarter in the Ravens' eventual 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday. On the second-to-last play of the first half, Jermaine Johnson II tackled Jackson, who appeared to twist his ankle. Jackson was having an impressive game up to that point, completing 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Huntley replaced Jackson in the third quarter and completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards. The Ravens did not score a single point in the final two quarters. "Snoop" has a 7-9 record as a starter and has scored 14 total touchdowns compared to 12 turnovers. 
The Ravens are 6-11 in the regular season without Jackson since he became the full-time starter. His durability has become a talking point, as Baltimore has won zero playoff games in seasons where Jackson missed time due to injuries. YearInjuryGames missed2026Ankle?2025Back12025Hamstring32022PCL sprain52021Ankle4Jackson's injury comes at a bad time, as the Ravens have to travel to take on one of the hottest teams in the NFL in prime time. Penix has brought some stability to the passing attack, as Drake London is averaging 145.0 receiving yards per game over the past two contests, but the real headliner for Atlanta's offense is running back Bijan Robinson.
Robinson ranks second in rushing yards per game (123.5) and scrimmage yards per game (153.5) entering Week 5. title: Eagles releasing veteran QB Andy Dalton, still unsettled at QB2 behind Jalen Hurts - CBS Sports
description: Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team
body:
Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026

    4:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles have made a surprise personnel move as they prepare for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. The team has released veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, according to multiple reports. Dalton, who will turn 39 later this month, was intercepted in his only pass attempt this season. It occurred in the end zone during the first half of Philadelphia's eventual Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears when Jalen Hurts temporarily left the game after getting hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson. 
Dalton's spot on the Eagles' depth chart will be replaced by Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton. McKee, a 2023 sixth-round pick, has made one start in the last two years. He has five career touchdown passes and one interception and has completed 61.4% of his passes. Payton, a fifth-round pick in this year's draft, has yet to play in a regular-season game.While the Eagles adjust their quarterback room, Dalton will begin his search for a new team. A three-time Pro Bowler, Dalton spent his first nine NFL seasons with the Bengals, with whom he helped lead to the playoffs five straight seasons from 2011-16. He has also spent time with the Saints, Bears and Panthers. 
In his career, Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns, and 152 interceptions. He has completed 62.6% of his passes. Where will Dalton end up next? Here are a few possible landing spots. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    VikingsMinnesota could use another backup quarterback after it traded JJ McCarthy to the Giants. In Dalton, the Vikings would have two veteran quarterbacks behind Kyler Murray, alongside Carson Wentz. Wentz played well earlier this season after Murray sustained an injury. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giants Speaking of the Giants, they could also use a veteran quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury. Jameis Winston is coming off his best game as a Giant, but it's safe to say that the Giants would still benefit from having another quarterback in the room. However, after acquiring JJ McCarthy, it's unlikely they're willing to make another move.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints This is a situation where Dalton could serve as a mentor for Tyler Shough, whose season so far has had its share of ups and downs. At this point, Shough does not have a mentor in the quarterback room. His current backup is Spencer Rattler, who is a year younger than he is. Dalton could be a valuable sounding board for a young room looking for some guidance.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dolphins Like New Orleans, Dalton could serve as a mentor in Miami for Malik Willis, who is currently entrenched in his first season as a full-time starter. Willis' current backup, Kyle McCord, is also in his first year with the Dolphins and has yet to play in an NFL regular-season game. But the question remains whether the tanking Dolphins would go after a quarterback now or get their pick during the 2027 NFL Draft. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TitansAnother team where Dalton could help a young quarterback find his footing. Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, is still growing as a starting quarterback. It's safe to assume that a player with Dalton's experience would help him with his continued development.

title: Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles to meet in Week 5: Did Giants make right choice between first-round linebackers? - CBS Sports
description: There might not have been a wrong answer for the Giants at pick No. 5 in the 2026 NFL Draft
body:
There might not have been a wrong answer for the Giants at pick No. 5 in the 2026 NFL Draft
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When the Washington Commanders host the New York Giants on Sunday, keep an eye on No. 52. Both of them.There is a striking parallel between the two teams: Both have a first-round rookie linebacker from Ohio State who wears the same number as the other. Giants standout Arvell Reese and burgeoning Commanders star Sonny Styles became the first college linebacker teammates to be selected in the top 10 of the same NFL Draft when they flew off the board in April. In Week 5, they go head-to-head.At the draft, the Giants were in the enviable position of having both Reese and Styles available to them at pick No. 5. There was immense debate prior to draft night about which player New York should select if both were up for grabs. After the event, a major question was whether they took the right one.In the end, there might not have been a wrong answer. The case for Arvell ReeseThat the Giants are off to a 3-1 start despite being without quarterback Jaxson Dart for nearly three full games is largely a credit to Reese and the defense. New York is a top-10 team in yards and points allowed through Week 4, and Reese is the engine that powers the unit. Not only does he pace the team with 33 tackles, but he also leads the entire league in solo stops with 26.
Reese is also fresh off the best game of his young career: a nine-tackle effort with one tackle for loss in a 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The NFL recognized him as the Week 4 Rookie of the Week after he became the fifth Giants rookie with three passes defended and an interception in one game.
The production is already game-changing. It is everything the Giants could have asked for when they used their first of two first-round picks on a linebacker. Reese's utility goes well beyond the numbers, though. His versatility proved to be a major asset across four games for a Giants defense that lost its top edge rusher, Brian Burns, for the season with a torn ACL. Reese's pass-rushing ability from the off-ball linebacker spot will be crucial the rest of the year as the Giants work to overcome the absence of Burns, who last year amassed 16.5 sacks in an All-Pro campaign.Reese is a more natural pass-rusher than Styles, which is an obvious asset, but at the draft, there was hesitation over whether he was the better pick. The Giants were already stocked at the edge rusher position with Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux providing both top-flight play in the starting lineup and enviable depth. With one of them out for the year, though, Reese is even more important to the unit than he already was. He is a linebacker first and likely always will be, but Reese can also play in the trenches. In his debut, even with Burns healthy, he aligned on the line of scrimmage on 11 of 52 snaps.
The case for Sonny StylesReese is exactly what the Giants hoped they were getting when they picked him. But who's to say Sonny Styles would not have been the same? He could have been just as impactful, had he been the No. 5 pick instead.When the Commanders upset the Seahawks in Week 3, Styles looked the part of a star in the making. He earned the NFC Defensive Player of the Week award for his efforts, which also made him the first rookie linebacker in franchise history with an interception, a forced fumble and multiple passes defended in one game.Styles' ability to wreak havoc in the backfield with inside pressure is also tremendous. He boasts the highest pressure rate among rookie defenders with at least 25 pass-rush snaps at 17.9%. The Commanders are about as aggressive as they come in pass defense with the second-highest blitz rate in the league, per Next Gen Stats, and Styles is a key figure in that scheme as they regularly rush him toward the quarterback.
And then there was this play, where Styles demolished Saquon Barkley en route to a sack.
While they attack the pocket from different angles, Styles and Reese are both impact pass-rushers. Perhaps the Giants would have been better off with Styles, given their depth on the edge.Styles has stepped up in the face of injuries just like Reese. Leo Chenal and Jordan Magee are both on injured reserve, leaving Styles, Frankie Luvu and Kain Medrano as the only three available inside linebackers. Not only that, but Styles routinely handles the defense's green-dot duties, relaying play calls to the rest of the unit as just a rookie. There is a chance he could have secured that job with the Giants, too, considering New York relies on 2026 newcomer Tremaine Edmunds to orchestrate the defense. Styles has a whole lot on his plate for someone with only four games of experience, and is not just getting by. He is thriving.
Verdict: It's a washIn hindsight, the Giants found themselves in a win-win position at the draft. With Reese and Styles as their targets, they could not have gone wrong. What both players displayed over the first four games of their professional careers proved that New York could have gone in either direction and come away with the same result, at least for the first month of the year. The final analysis will not be complete for years, when their career arcs take full shape, but as of now, the Ohio State products are on level footing.If the argument for Reese was that he is the better pass rusher, then Styles bridged the gap with his effective blitzes. If the argument for Styles was that he is the better defender in coverage, then Reese closed that discrepancy. According to Pro Football Focus, Reese graded out over four games as the ninth-best linebacker in coverage, while Styles is a mere six spots ahead of him at No. 3. In a sample size of 74 qualified linebackers, both are excellent.Both are top-five rookie linebackers in overall PFF defensive grade.Rookie LBPFF Defensive GradeHarold Perkins Jr., Falcons82.6Josiah Trotter, Buccaneers79.2Arvell Reese, Giants77.1Sonny Styles, Commanders76.9Jaishawn Barham, Cowboys69.1Reese has the second-best odds to win Defensive Rookie of the Year at +275, and Styles is directly behind him with the third-shortest odds at +750, per DraftKings. The margin between their first-year production is extremely thin, and both carry long-term stardom potential. The Giants ought to feel elated about their choice in the draft, and the Commanders should, too.

        USC wide receiver Terrell Anderson will undergo season-ending surgery, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Anderson was a huge pick-up for the Trojans in the transfer portal, but his season is over after just three games and two receptions for 50 yards.A four-star recruit coming out of high school, Anderson spent the first two seasons of his college career at NC State, where he broke out as a sophomore in 2025. Last fall, Anderson totaled 39 receptions for 629 yards and five touchdowns.When Anderson entered the portal, there was plenty of interest in him, given his unique combination of size and skill. He was ranked as the No. 10 overall transfer, according to 247Sports. When the Trojans signed Anderson, he was viewed as a potential superstar with Jayden Maiava throwing him the football.
Unfortunately for Maiava and the Trojans, the injury has impacted Anderson throughout the season. He missed the season-opener against Fresno State, and he played only sparingly in the last three games. Anderson recorded two receptions for 50 yards in a loss to Oregon, but that's the only time he appeared on the stat sheet outside of punt returns.
With Anderson on the shelf for the remainder of the season, USC will need production from other players in the passing game, but the receiver room has been banged up in the early going.Injury bug biting USC pass-catchersAnderson isn't the only key receiver who has dealt with injuries in Los Angeles. Freshman wideout Trent Mosley got off to a terrific start with 255 yards and four touchdowns in three games. However, he's been sidelined for the last two games after suffering a knee injury.Freshman tight end Mark Bowman, the No. 42 overall player in the 2026 signing class, is also dealing with an injury after missing the Washington game last week. Bowman has 21 catches for 204 yards and two touchdowns through four games.
Mosley and Bowman are both listed as questionable for Saturday night's road game against Penn State.With Anderson, Mosley and Bowman all less than 100 percent, receivers Zach Williams and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt will be asked to pick up some of the slack. Williams and Dixon-Wyatt currently lead the team in receiving, and they'll get plenty of targets in Happy Valley.Sophomore wideout Tanook Hines will also factor into the equation, and he made an exceptional touchdown catch against the Huskies last weekend. If Hines continues to elevate his game, that would make the loss of Anderson -- and the rest of the offensive injuries -- easier to overcome.

title: Arteta says conscious clear over time at Manchester City - CBS Sports
description: Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's allege
body:
Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's alleged rule breaches to focus on turning his side into the best in the world
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arsenal have spent the last week talking themselves up as the coming force in world football, a club who believe they can be the best in the game for years to come and are prepared to say so repeatedly. Their manager, the only man in the Premier League with a winners' medal in his back pocket, has just put pen to paper on a contract that will extend his spell for a decade.And that was at best this week's B plot. Such is the gravitational pull of the Manchester City story. It is one that Mikel Arteta was always going to find himself drawn into. No manager can say they have experienced a Premier League warped by City quite like Arteta. As a player, he arrived at the Emirates Stadium a week after Samir Nasri had upped sticks for the Etihad. His coaching career began under Pep Guardiola, two of his three and a half years as an assistant falling within the period of the 114 breaches of Premier League rules. Then, of course, came the defining period of his career so far, the long and ultimately glorious battle against City for Premier League supremacy.There was plenty Arteta might have shared. Little he chose to. Ultimately, the nearest he got to a definitive statement on City was when asked, given his time at the club, whether his conscience was clear. "Yes," he said emphatically. That aside, the Spaniard was even more cagey on his former employers than he would be when asked about a high-profile injury. It was easy to see why Arteta might be reticent to speak for a club that has reserved the right to explore legal avenues against City once the Premier League's case has been concluded. He was no more candid, however, when it came to reflecting his own personal experience of that momentous day in Premier League history when the charges dropped."This has been going for various years," he said. "That process is still not finished. So it is very difficult to express how I feel, because it is not resolved. When it is resolved, I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel."
He will be held to that. Few came to London Colney expecting Arteta to expound on the City situation. Even if it weren't for his ties to the Etihad, it is just not his style to concern himself with many matters beyond his team, the crusade for more substitutes on the bench notwithstanding. The media room gravitas of reigning Premier League champion does not sit as easily on Arteta as it did, for instance, on Jurgen Klopp, let alone Arsene Wenger.Arteta was not the only one to play the many questions over City with a dead bat (this is a cricket reference for all you Americans out there). Andoni Iraola was similarly circumspect, ahead of his side's confrontation with City this weekend, though it was notable that Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, who might have had more Premier League winners' medals had it not been for City's rule-breaking, called for speed in concluding this process. That is a view shared by many other clubs in the Premier League, though on Friday's evidence Arteta was in no rush to resume questions over his past.His future seemed far more invigorating now that he is signed up to 2030. An extension to terms due to expire at the end of this season had long been expected; what was more notable was the way in which club and manager reached an agreement to prolong their partnership beyond the decade mark. Even when they end with one being the best-paid manager in the Premier League, few managers find themselves saying that they "loved" the negotiations after fresh terms have been agreed. Arteta is different.
He loved "the way we have analysed what we've done together and especially how we're going to take this club to be the best in the world for many years... You just have a sense how you feel about each other, how we do things, and I feel really lucky and having [co-chairs] Stan and Josh [Kroenke] in front of you and talking to them and expressing still what they want to do, how they want to do it, especially is just inspiring."That is not the first time since signing his new deal that Arteta has set expectations at a stratospheric level. Last season's Premier League title was, he said, just the beginning. Meanwhile, club chief executive Richard Garlick spoke about Arsenal "[dominating] football for the next number of years". That is a big ask for a team with one top-flight title to their name in 22 years, one that is still without that Champions League win that is a prerequisite of elite status. These are also the sort of lines that can come back to haunt a team, and yet Arteta is not afraid of setting the bar at the highest level."I don't think you have to hide it; the thing is that you have to earn it every single day. Your aspirations and your dreams are where they are. I think it's easier to get them [now]. If I said to you the one that I had when I arrived [as manager in 2019], probably you would say what are you talking about? 
"That was the ambition, that's the drive, and it's because we believe that we can do it, and then there will be many factors that would allow us or not to achieve it. Time will tell, but certainly that drive is there."And of course that opportunity to establish Arsenal as the leading lights in England and Europe is all the greater with their rivals facing what seems likely to be a cataclysmic set of sanctions. Not, of course, that Arteta would want to discuss it in those terms.

        Serie A is finally back this weekend after the long international break, and all the top teams will be involved in the fight, with AS Roma traveling to Como for the most anticipated match of the weekend. Elsewhere, Inter will host Parma at San Siro on Saturday while AC Milan will face Sassuolo on Sunday, a few hours before the Juventus away game against Cagliari. Let's now take a closer look at what to watch for on Matchday 6: the game, the player, the stat and the story you need to know.Game to watch: Como vs. AS RomaOn Sunday, Como will host AS Roma at the Stadio Sinigaglia for another exciting Serie A game. Cesc Fabregas will try to stop Gian Piero Gasperini's side, who drew at home against Inter in their last game before the break. AS Roma are now considered a solid Scudetto contender after four wins and a draw in their opening five matches, and they currently lead the standings tied on points with Inter and Lazio, one of the surprises of the Serie A season. Como, on the other hand, are once again showing why they should be considered a serious candidate for the top four, with one of the most interesting and exciting sporting projects around Europe. Como and AS Roma will also return to Champions League action next week. The Giallorossi host Real Madrid on Wednesday, marking Jose Mourinho's first return to the Stadio Olimpico since leaving Roma in 2024. Meanwhile, Como face Feyenoord away from home.Player to watch: Christian PulisicUnited States men's national team forward Christian Pulisic wasn't called up by Mauricio Pochettino for the last international break, as he was still not at his best. Pulisic started the new season late, as he was recovering from the injury suffered at the 2026 World Cup. He scored his first goal of the season against Lecce before the break. Things will be different this weekend, with Pulisic now fully available to AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim.  Stat of the weekend: Christian Pulisic was back on the scoresheet, 266 days after his last Serie A goal (Dec. 28, 2025, against Verona). Let's say a driver is priced at -150 to win the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7th, and the next best driver has +200 odds. That means the driver at -150 is a decent favorite to win, and you'd have to risk $150 to win $100. The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.Below are DraftKings Sportsbook's odds for the NASCAR Cup Series Bank of America 400.
